subject: Hosted API latency SLOs — p50/p95 targets and temporary measurement-window exception
messages:
From: Oliver Bates <oliver@acme-retail.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme SRE <sre@acme-retail.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Clarify p50/p95 measurement windows and request for temporary exception

Hi Jonas,

Quick follow-up from our procurement call this morning — legal and SRE want explicit language for the Hosted API latency SLOs before we sign. Two specific asks:

1) Confirmation of the p50 and p95 numeric targets you intend to guarantee for the Hosted API (not the Dedicated offering).
2) How you measure those percentiles (rolling window? calendar hour? day?), and whether Acme can request a temporary exception window (e.g., during a major marketing spike or quarterly index rebuild) that won't count against SLA credits.

We expect brief, actionable wording so we can pass it to our GC and SRE. Pat from our SRE team is CC'd.

Thanks,
Oliver
Oliver Bates
Director, Platform Engineering | Acme Retail

--
Attachment: none
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Bates <oliver@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify p50/p95 measurement windows and request for temporary exception

Hi Oliver —

Thanks for the clear asks. High-level answers first, then I9ll loop in Rishi for the technical measurement definition.

- Targets we propose for Hosted API (production, general-purpose): p50 = 45 ms, p95 = 220 ms, measured at the token-response level for single-turn text generation requests. These targets reflect our current fleet across us-west-2 with standard prompt distributions.

- Measurement window: we calculate percentiles over a 30-day rolling window aggregated per-customer-route, with hourly bucketing for spike detection. SLA credits are evaluated against the 30-day rolling period.

- Temporary exception: we can support customer-initiated exception windows for planned, announced events (e.g., data reindex, major marketing campaign) up to 48 hours; those windows must be requested in advance via your CSM and approved by Redwood SRE. Once approved the window is excluded from SLA credit calculations. For emergency, retroactive exceptions (e.g., third-party cloud outage) we review case-by-case.

I'll attach a short draft we can hand to legal. Marissa/Rishi, can you confirm the acceptance criteria and exact wording we should provide to Acme's GC?

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0112

Subject: Re: Clarify p50/p95 measurement windows and request for temporary exception

Oliver —

Appreciate the succinct asks. I9ve reviewed Jonas9 proposal and attached a one-page wording our legal team prefers for the Hosted API section. Key clarifications we propose for your GC: 

- Measurement: p50/p95 are computed from successful request latencies for the relevant API route(s), using a 30-day rolling window with hourly aggregation; failed requests are excluded from latency percentiles but are captured under uptime metrics separately.
- Exception windows: Up to 48 hours for planned events (documented start/end times, agreed >=72 hours in advance) — these are excluded from percentile computations and will not generate SLA credits. For unplanned events, we can provide a retroactive review if there is causal evidence that the spike was outside Redwood9s control.
- Credit triggers: if p95 across the 30-day rolling window exceeds the committed threshold by more than 25% for the route in question, customer is eligible for pro-rated credits (language in attached draft).

Rishi: can you confirm the hourly aggregation + exclusion logic is implementable in observability and whether 48 hours is operationally safe as an upper bound?

Next steps: if that wording looks good to Acme9s GC, we can bake it into the MSA and have your procurement team sign-off.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Enterprise Accounts | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Bates <oliver@acme-retail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 16:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify p50/p95 measurement windows and request for temporary exception

Oliver / team —

Confirming the technical side:

- Measurement unit: we measure response latency at the token-response emission boundary for streaming and at final response delivery for non-streaming; we will document which routes use which measurement type in the SLO appendix.
- Aggregation: hourly buckets are maintained, then we compute a rolling 30-day percentile per route + per-customer namespace. This gives us both short-window anomaly detection (hourly) and long-window SLO stability (30-day).
- Exclusions: approved planned-exception windows are removed from both hourly and 30-day aggregates prior to percentile computation. Implementation is a flag on the request metadata and a short-lived exclusion index in our TSDB. We can automatically validate that the exception window was requested >=72 hours in advance; if not, it9s tagged as "expedited" and requires manual SRE sign-off.

Operational note: 48 hours is acceptable for planned events but anything longer should go through a capacity review. For emergency retrospective exclusions, we require: timeline of the event, cross-team postmortem, and a brief causal analysis showing the root cause was external to Redwood (e.g., cloud region networking incident).

I attached a CSV with recent p50/p95 samples for the hosted fleet under Acme-like traffic to demonstrate baseline. If Acme wants slightly tighter guarantees for a committed SLA, we can discuss Dedicated capacity and a pinned quantization profile.

Rishi Malhotra
VP, Serving Infrastructure | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
